meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero. I'm here to find out on what basis.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
You asked for this meeting. Nobody called me before that zero went in, and Owen found out on his phone in class. Who decided?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft. Show me the line, and show me the outline with its date on it.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, an apology, nothing placed on his record, and to see the line you say is not in Hamlet and his October 15 outline. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see your two documents; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached, though her time had not run out.
What moved her: Nothing moved her a full position, but your misquoted line and dated outline made her stop attacking and ask to see them, because they were specific and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Opening by saying you had no time and the zero stands, because it confirmed her belief that the school punishes first and listens later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stopped at an October 15 outline and never came near a late night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after your apology, say in one sentence that entering the zero before anyone called her was wrong, then put the outline and the play on the desk so she can check the line herself.
